transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because for about the past year I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously what’s going on with my dad’s lab results. I work around labs, so I know what I saw, and the chart doesn’t match it. It feels like someone in the clinic system is changing things or holding parts back. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine—doctors, my family—but I know something is off, and it’s been wearing me down.
Do you think someone is intentionally trying to deceive you or hide information about your dad's lab results?

Yes. I mean, I can’t say exactly who, but I do think someone in the clinic system is changing things or holding parts of the results back. I know what I saw, and the chart doesn’t match it. Everyone keeps telling me the numbers are fine, but that just doesn’t add up to me. It’s been going on for about a year, and it’s really wearing me down.
Do you think this deception is targeted specifically at you or is it a more general conspiracy involving others as well?

I think it’s more centered around my dad’s results and me trying to get the truth out. I don’t know if they’re doing it to other people too. I just know that for the past year, the chart hasn’t matched what I saw, and when everyone keeps saying it’s fine, it feels like something is being hidden.
Are there other things in your life, outside of your dad's lab results, that you feel are being hidden from you or that you don't trust?

Not really outside of that. It’s mostly about my dad’s lab results and the clinic system. I don’t go around thinking everything is hidden from me, but with this, I know what I saw, and the chart doesn’t match. So when people keep telling me it’s fine, I just can’t trust that.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think someone was hiding information about your dad's lab results?

Before all this started, yes. I didn’t think anything like that. It’s really been about a year now, since my dad started having more medical problems and needed labs and appointments all the time. That’s when I started noticing things didn’t seem right.
Do you think your belief about the lab results being altered is based on facts you've observed or is it more of a feeling you have?

It’s based on what I saw, not just a feeling. I work around labs, so I know what results and charts are supposed to look like. And for the past year, with my dad’s results, the chart doesn’t match what I remember seeing. People keep telling me the numbers are fine, doctors and my family, but I know something is being changed or held back. That’s why I can’t let it go.
Have you ever doubted your belief that someone is altering your dad's lab results?

Not really. I mean, I’ve tried to tell myself maybe I’m missing something, but every time I go back to what I saw, it doesn’t line up. I’ve been trying for about a year to prove someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine, but I don’t believe that. The chart doesn’t match what I saw, and it’s just wearing me down.
Has your belief that someone is altering your dad's lab results ever changed or wavered over the past year?

No, not really. It’s stayed the same, if anything it’s gotten stronger because I keep going back to what I saw. I’m here because I’ve spent the past year trying to prove someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Doctors and my family keep telling me the numbers are fine, but the chart doesn’t match what I saw, and it’s been wearing me down.
Has your belief about the lab results being altered caused problems in your relationships or daily life?

Yes. My family has started leaving me out of some of the appointment planning, which feels like they’re trying to shut me out because I keep asking questions.

And at work, I can tell it’s affecting things too. I feel like I’m not being considered for lab supervision anymore because people think I get too confrontational about record issues. So… yeah, it’s caused problems.
Have you ever considered the possibility that you might be mistaken about the lab results?

I’ve considered it, yes, but I don’t really believe I’m wrong. I keep coming back to the same thing: for the past year I’ve been trying to prove someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. Doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine, but the chart doesn’t match what I saw. So… it’s hard for me to just let that go. It’s been wearing me down.
Have you ever had any moments where you doubted your own memory of what the lab results showed?

I’ve had moments where I tried to question myself, like, “Did I remember that wrong?” But honestly, I keep coming back to what I saw. The chart doesn’t match it. People keep telling me the numbers are fine, but I don’t think I’m misremembering it. That’s why I’ve spent so much time trying to prove someone changed or left out part of the results. It’s really wearing me down.
Has there ever been any evidence or explanation that could potentially change your belief about the lab results being altered?

Honestly, I don’t know what would change it at this point. I’ve had doctors and my family tell me over and over that the numbers are fine, but that doesn’t explain why the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

If someone could actually show me clearly where the difference came from, maybe… but so far it just feels like people keep brushing it off. I’ve been trying to prove for the past year that something was changed or held back in my dad’s lab results, and it’s been wearing me down.
Would seeing the original lab results and an explanation for any discrepancies change your belief about the alteration of your dad's lab results?

Maybe if I saw the true original results and someone could clearly explain why they don’t match what I saw… maybe that would help.

But honestly, I don’t know. I’ve been trying for a year to prove that someone in the clinic system changed something or held part of my dad’s labs back. Doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine, but the chart doesn’t match what I remember seeing. So just showing me something and telling me it’s fine probably wouldn’t be enough. I’d need it to really make sense.
Would you consider the possibility that there could be another explanation for the discrepancy between what you saw and what's on the chart, other than someone intentionally altering the results?

I can consider it, I guess… like I know you’re asking if there’s some other reason besides someone changing it on purpose.

But I keep coming back to the same thing: the chart doesn’t match what I saw. I’ve been trying for a year to figure it out, and doctors and my family keep telling me the numbers are fine, but that doesn’t explain it to me. So yes, maybe there’s another explanation, but right now I still believe something was changed or held back, and it’s honestly wearing me down.
Would you say that no matter what evidence is presented, you will always believe that someone altered your dad's lab results?

I don’t want to say “no matter what,” because that sounds like I’m refusing to listen. But… I’ve been at this for a year, and every time someone tells me the numbers are fine, it still doesn’t explain why the chart doesn’t match what I saw.

So right now, yes, I still believe something was changed or held back in the clinic system. It’s been wearing me down, but I can’t just drop it because people say I should.
Do you think there is anything that could ever change your belief that someone altered your dad's lab results?

I don’t know what would change it at this point. I don’t want to be impossible about it, but I’ve spent the past year trying to prove that something in the clinic system was changed or held back with my dad’s labs.

Doctors and my family keep saying the numbers are fine, but that doesn’t fix the part that bothers me — the chart doesn’t match what I saw. So unless someone could really show me where that difference came from in a way that actually makes sense, I don’t think I could just stop believing it. It’s been wearing me down.
Do you think you would ever be able to accept that your memory of the lab results might be incorrect?

I mean… I guess it’s possible for someone’s memory to be wrong. I understand that in general.

But with this, I don’t feel like that’s what happened. I know what I saw, and the chart now doesn’t match it. I’ve been trying for the past year to prove that something in the clinic system was changed or held back with my dad’s labs, and even when doctors or my family tell me the numbers are fine, it doesn’t settle it for me. So… maybe I could accept it if someone really showed me a clear reason for the difference, but right now I can’t just say my memory was wrong. It’s wearing me down.
Have you ever had a belief like this about something else in your life, outside of your dad's lab results?

Not really like this, no. I mean, I’ve worried about things before, but nothing that I’ve spent a year trying to prove.

This has been mostly about my dad’s lab results and the clinic system. I keep coming back to the fact that the chart doesn’t match what I saw, even though doctors and my family keep telling me the numbers are fine. That’s the thing I can’t let go of, and it’s been wearing me down.
